description: Hold NIFTY MIDCAP150 MOMENTUM 50 only while it is at or above its own 200-session average, sized by a 20% a year volatility target over 60 sessions. Decided weekly as five weekday parts, so exposure moves in steps.
hypothesis: The two guards act on different things. The trend filter steps out of long bear markets like 2008, and the volatility target cuts size in sudden crashes like 2020 before the trend turns. Together they held the fall to 26% at a 15% target but kept too little invested. A looser 20% target keeps more money invested in calm recoveries, which should lift return to about 1.5% a month while the trend filter still keeps the fall near 30%.
lessons: Midcap150 momentum-50 with a volatility target controls the fall well, with lots of headroom (29.5% vs 59.5% for the benchmark). The binding constraint is return, not risk. Return is lost to cash drag (70% invested, beta 0.44) and to whipsaws in mild bull years (2016, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2025). The volatility target can afford to be looser. Do not tighten risk controls further on this idea. If loosening the target pushes the fall past the limit, the 2008 and 2011 rows will show it. Second-half alpha decay (5.66%) is worth watching.

description: Hold NIFTY MIDCAP150 MOMENTUM 50 and NIFTY SMALLCAP250 MOMENTUM QUALITY 100 at half the account each. Each half goes to cash while its index is below its own 200-session average. The whole book is scaled to a 25% yearly volatility target measured over 60 sessions. Decided weekly.
hypothesis: The single-index plan (MM50, own 200-day average, vol target 25-30%) is already inside the fall limit and at about 1.5% a month. Its t of 2.56 falls short because all of its excess return comes from one index's idiosyncratic path. A second high-return index with a different size segment and a quality tilt (SC250 MQ100, 17.8% a year, t 1.68) should diversify that residual noise. Its own trend filter will often switch at a different time than MM50's, so exposure moves in half-steps, which loses less to the four-part blurring. Lower combined volatility also lets the vol target stay more invested during recoveries. This should lift t without giving up return, while 2008 and 2020 stay governed by the trend filters.
lessons: Midcap/smallcap momentum+quality pairing beats the bench mainly through drawdown avoidance and midcap bull years. It loses in years when smallcaps lag large caps (2016, 2018-19, 2022, 2025), and that kills the t-stat. Next day, try a regime filter on relative strength of midcap vs large-cap index (hold large-cap quality when mid/small lags) rather than plain cash. The return gap is small (0.05%/mo); the luck check is the harder one.
